title: Normalize batch Frechet mean weights independently
body:
## Problem

Batch gradient descent divides every weighted tangent sum by the number of observations. Rescaling one batch's weights therefore changes its effective step size and stopping criterion, even though its weighted mean is unchanged. Small component masses in Riemannian EM can stop at an inaccurate mean, while large scales can overshoot.

## Change

Normalize each batch's weight column once by its own sum, without modifying caller data. Then form the tangent mean directly from those normalized weights. Use a safe divisor for an all-zero column so the existing multi-sample zero-weight behavior stays finite. The unweighted case has the same mathematical update as before.

## Validation

On unchanged base `2fc8e25eb8955767292552f9c0c1438be362ba8f`, the same 13 regression/control cases report **7 failures and 6 passes** on both NumPy and Autograd. Independent Euclidean/matrix weighted-average and Poincaré-diameter analytic oracles cover batch-specific scales from 1e-6 to 1e6, zero-weight controls, and preservation of caller points and weights. A real one-iteration Riemannian EM fit verifies a low-mass component's mean against all of its posterior weights.

At source `f9a632e5f79bf523f9439ef694c1fd2e6a96d2cd`, the learning and adjacent geometry test scope reports:

- NumPy: **1,115 passed, 5 skipped, 548 deselected, 5 xfailed, 4 xpassed**.
- Autograd: **1,117 passed, 3 skipped, 548 deselected, 5 xfailed, 4 xpassed**.
- Ruff and applicable pre-commit hooks pass; the exact validated checkout remains clean.

[Exact-source CI](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43673754415). Python 3.13.18, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and Autograd 1.9.1. Existing slow/redundant markers are excluded; the full repository and PyTorch backend were not run.

## Scope and related work

The regression scope uses nonnegative weights. The pre-existing single-observation fast path and signed-weight validation are unchanged. This patch changes weight scaling in the batch optimizer; it does not change EM density normalization or component axes.

Reviewed all six prior author PRs and all 50 pre-existing fork heads. Forty-nine contain the unnormalized batch update; one predates the batch algorithm. Reviewed actual related changes including #1873 (refactor), #2156 (logging), and #2138 (input ownership in GeometricMedian and MDM). None implements per-batch weight normalization.
